questions.question: Why isn't token streaming enough for an agent?
options: Most of an agent's time goes to tool calls and tool waits, which produce no text tokens
questions.explanation: In the live run, step 1 produced only a tool call. A token-only stream showed nothing for 2 seconds.

questions.question: Why is a tool_call event yielded only once the call is complete, while text is yielded per fragment?
options: A partial tool call can't be run; partial text is still useful to show
questions.explanation: Arguments arrive in fragments; only the merged, complete JSON can be executed.

questions.question: Two tool calls stream interleaved. How does merge_tool_deltas keep them apart?
options: It can't; parallel calls are unsupported
questions.explanation: Every fragment carries the index of the call it belongs to.

questions.question: The user clicks Stop while the agent is mid-run. In this lesson's design, what stops further model calls?
options: A global flag checked by every tool
The consumer calls close() on the generator, which raises GeneratorExit at the paused yield
questions.explanation: Generators stop when closed. No polling or flags needed.

questions.question: In the live run, the final answer was complete at 11.9 s. When did the user first see text?
questions.explanation: With an event stream, the tool call showed at 2.0 s and the answer started at 2.6 s.

questions.question: Ollama sent llama3.2's tool call as a single chunk, while hosted APIs send arguments in pieces. What does that mean for your code?
options: Merge fragments by index anyway; one complete chunk is just the simplest case
questions.explanation: The fragment-merging code handles one chunk and many chunks the same way.
